samples.summary: serve() accepts `fault` but never forwards it to observeAction, so the seeded fault is silently inert for every explorer session
samples.evidence: `serve(browser, baseUrl, timeoutMs, fault = null)` (line 415) is the only consumer of `--fault` in serve mode, yet its call at line 447 is `await observeAction(page, req.action, { baseUrl, timeoutMs: …, oracles, index: index++ })` — `fault` is not in the options object. `runAction`'s goto only appends `&fault=` when it receives a non-null `fault` (line 244), so a serve-mode `goto` always navigates to the CLEAN route. The whole explorer path uses serve mode: hunt-ui.mjs `runHunt` → `exploreUi(..., { fault })` → `openUiSession({ repoRoot, fault })` (hunt-ui-session.mjs:118 spawns `--serve --fault <id>`). Consequence: `node hunt-ui.mjs run --fault drop-second-char` prints "FAULT INJECTION ACTIVE (?fault=…) — this run is a positive control" (hunt-ui.mjs, runHunt) while the explorer drives an unmodified app; the run reports nothing and looks like a healthy funnel. The end-to-end positive control this PR exists to add therefore does not work through the live-session path (only the plan/replay path, which forwards it at runner line 472). Nothing in scripts/agent/*.test.mjs asserts serve forwards the fault.

samples.summary: `record.prediction.verdict` is always "unknown" — runner observations carry no `verdict` field
samples.evidence: `verdict: failing?.verdict ?? "unknown"` reads `failing` from `runPlanImpl(...)[0][cand.failingIndex]`, i.e. an observation produced by `observeAction` in hunt-ui-runner.mjs, which returns `{index, action, ok, error, value, actual, actualError, oracles}` and deliberately never computes a verdict ("The runner does NOT compare", runner line ~355; grep for `verdict` in packages/frontend/scripts finds no producer). The verdict is only ever produced by `assessExpectation` inside hunt-ui-tool.mjs and stored on the JOURNAL entry (`entry.prediction`), not on the replayed observation. So every reported finding renders `- **prediction:** … — unknown` at hunt-ui.mjs:564. The unit test passes only because its fixture (`FUNNEL_OBS` in hunt-ui.test.mjs) hand-adds a `verdict` field the pipeline never produces.

samples.summary: uiCitationsOf concatenates every verifier's groundedIn without de-duplication, so N verifiers repeating one location can satisfy a `minCitations` of N
samples.evidence: `uiCitationsOf` returns `verdicts.flatMap(v => v.groundedIn)`. The gate's step 4 counts `cites.length < minCitations` (hunt-gate.mjs:549-550) over that flat list, so with two verifiers each citing the SAME `file:line`, a persona configured with `minCitations: 2` is satisfied by a single distinct location — the check no longer means what its name says. Latent today (both shipped personas use `minCitations: 1`) but it also makes `record.groundedIn` contain duplicates, which the report renders verbatim.

samples.summary: `--surface` values are validated AFTER selection, so a typo fails with the misleading "no personas selected"
samples.evidence: In cmdRun: `const { selected: personas, excluded } = selectPersonas(all, { charter: args.charter, surface: args.surface }); if (personas.length === 0) fail("no personas selected");` runs BEFORE the loop `for (const s of args.surface) { if (!UI_SURFACES.includes(s)) fail("--surface … is not one of …") }`. `--surface docs` therefore excludes every persona and exits with "no personas selected" — precisely the zero-that-reads-as-clean failure the rest of the file works to avoid — instead of naming the invalid surface. Ordering the validation first fixes it.

samples.summary: exploreUi can close the same session twice when a retry attempt fails before assigning `live`
samples.evidence: The retry closure begins `await live?.session.close();` and only later reassigns `live = { journal, budget, session }`. If `openSession` (or the code before the assignment) throws on a retried attempt, `live` still references the previous, already-closed session, and the outer `finally { await live?.session.close(); }` closes it a second time. Harmless if `close()` is idempotent, but the second close is also the only close that ever runs for that attempt — a session opened and then failing inside `createServerImpl` before assignment would leak instead.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `serve()` (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:415) receives `fault` from main (line 523) but its sole `observeAction` call (lines 447-452) omits `fault` from the options object, so `observeAction`'s default `fault = null` (line 332) is used and `runAction` (line 336) sees null. Line 244 is the only place the fault becomes a URL parameter (`&fault=`), so every serve-mode `goto` navigates to the clean route — verified there is no other injection mechanism (no env var, no boot hook, `openPage`/`waitForReady` do not touch it). The live explorer path is serve mode end to end: hunt-ui.mjs:938 → exploreUi → openSession({repoRoot, fault}) (hunt-ui.mjs:307) → hunt-ui-session.mjs:111-121 spawns `--serve ... --fault <id>`. Meanwhile hunt-ui.mjs:922-923 prints "FAULT INJECTION ACTIVE ... this run is a positive control", so the run announces an active seeded defect while driving an unmodified app — a fail-quiet inversion. The plan/replay path forwards it correctly (runAttempt, line 472), which confirms the intended contract and isolates the omission. No guard or caller compensates; this is a dropped-argument logic bug that breaks the feature's core flow, squarely in the correctness lane.
